title: Finite flat modules over finite type algebras over valuation rings are finitely presented
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Let $A\to B$ be a ring map of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $M$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. If $M$ is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $M$ is finitely presented as a $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 053E (lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation), part (2), statement and proof at lines 5966--6001

proof.text: First $A$ is local. Indeed its fraction-field characterization [def-trf-valuation-ring] implies that any two nonzero elements $a,b\in A$ satisfy $a\mid b$ or $b\mid a$, by applying it to $a/b$. Thus its nonunits form a proper ideal: if $a,b$ are nonunits and $b=ac$, then $a+b=a(1+c)$ is a nonunit; the other divisibility and zero cases are identical, and multiplication preserves nonunits. Every proper ideal contains only nonunits, so this is the unique maximal ideal. Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and module generators $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ of $M$ over $B$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: For $d\geq0$ let $F_dM$ be the $A$-span of $b_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots b_n^{\alpha_n}m_j$ with $\sum_i\alpha_i\leq d$. Then $F_dM\subseteq F_{d+1}M$, $b_iF_dM\subseteq F_{d+1}M$, and $\bigcup_dF_dM=M$, by the chosen generators. Put $N=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}F_dM\,t^d$, viewed as the $A$-module of finite formal polynomials with degree-$d$ coefficient in $F_dM$. For the polynomial ring $P=A[X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $X_0$ act by $t$ and $X_i$ by $b_it$. These commuting $A$-linear actions define a $P$-module, graded by polynomial degree. It is generated over $P$ by the $m_jt^0$: the spanning term $b^\alpha m_jt^d$ equals $X_0^{d-|\alpha|}X_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots X_n^{\alpha_n}(m_jt^0)$.

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: The flat $A$-module $M$ is torsion-free by [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], since $A$ is a domain. If $0\ne a\in A$ and $a\sum_dx_dt^d=0$ in $N$, each $ax_d=0$ in $M$, hence every $x_d=0$. Thus $N$ is torsion-free as an $A$-module. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] to deduce that $N$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-graded-flat-module-finite-presentation] with coefficient ring $R=A$, polynomial ring $P$ with all $n+1$ variables of weight $1$, and graded module $L=N$ (zero in negative degrees). Step 1 gives locality of $A$, Step 2 gives the internal grading and finite generation, and Step 3 gives flatness over $A$. Hence $N$ is finitely presented over $P$.

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: Evaluation $\epsilon:N\to M$, $\sum_dx_dt^d\mapsto\sum_dx_d$, is $P$-linear for the action $X_0\mapsto1$, $X_i\mapsto b_i$ on $M$, and is surjective because $\bigcup_dF_dM=M$. Its kernel is $(X_0-1)N$: if $\sum_{d=0}^Dx_d=0$, put $y_d=-\sum_{i=0}^dx_i\in F_dM$ for $0\leq d<D$. Direct multiplication gives $(t-1)\sum_{d=0}^{D-1}y_dt^d=\sum_{d=0}^Dx_dt^d$. For $D=0$ the kernel element is zero. Conversely evaluation kills $(t-1)N$. Therefore $N/(X_0-1)N\cong M$, with the stated action of every variable.

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: Write the finite presentation from Step 4 as $N=P^v/\langle h_1,\ldots,h_u\rangle_P$, using [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Put $Q=A[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$. Evaluation $X_0=1$ identifies $P/(X_0-1)$ with $Q$ by the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Quotienting $N$ by $(X_0-1)N$ gives $P^v/(\langle h_1,\ldots,h_u\rangle_P+(X_0-1)P^v)$, which is $Q^v/\langle h_1(1,X),\ldots,h_u(1,X)\rangle_Q$: the coordinate quotient map has kernel $(X_0-1)P^v$, and sends the relation span onto exactly that evaluated span. Step 5 identifies this quotient with $M$. Thus $M$ is finitely presented over $Q$.

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: The map $Q\to B$, $X_i\mapsto b_i$, is surjective by the algebra generators of Step 1. In particular $B$ is of finite type as a $Q$-algebra (no further generators). The $Q$-action on $M$ in Step 6 is restriction of its given $B$-action, as checked on each $X_i$ in Step 5. Apply [lem-trf-finitely-presented-over-subring] to $Q\to B$ and $M$: finite presentation over $Q$ from Step 6 implies finite presentation over $B$.
